title: Identifying Emotional States using Keystroke Dynamics

dataset.name: Not explicitly reported.
dataset.type_source: Field study using an experience-sampling methodology (ESM)

experimental_conditions.data_collection: Data collected in situ during daily computer activities via custom software running in the background
text_conditions: Fixed text entered from Alice's Adventures in Wonderland

proposed_method.name: Decision tree (C4.5) with supervised attribute selection and under-sampling
proposed_method.description: A C4.5 decision tree was used with correlation-based feature subset selection and under-sampling for emotional-state classification.

primary_performance.experimental_condition: Sadness detection using fixed-text keystroke dynamics with 2 class levels (agree vs. disagree) and under-sampling

third_evaluation_field.scope: Extracted across single keys, digraphs, and trigraphs

evidence.statement: From the raw keystroke data, we extracted a number of features derived mainly from key duration (dwell time) and key latency (flight time).

dataset.statement: Due to the large variations in the number of responses per user, we did not create user-specific models, but aggregated the data across participants for 1129 valid instances.
